brief.title: Your trip at a glance
brief.text:
A private expedition on the Sea of Cortez, built around the wind. Kite is the center of the trip: the best wind windows come first, and sailing, swimming, meals and rest fit around them.

While she rides with Lou, he can head out on his wing. Eagle Ray Expeditions brings the boat, the crew, the kitchen and the logistics, so the only thing you plan is when to get in the water.

facts.text: Open dates in the kite season, December to April
Captain, chef and Lou as Expedition Leader
Kite gear for her included, his wing gear welcome on board
Airport pickup and private transfer included

about.title: La Ventana with Lou
about.text:
This is going to be a different way to kite. Instead of a session on the beach and the rest of the day somewhere else, we will live it on the water: kiting with the wind and, in between, good food, swimming, paddleboarding, and sunsets and sunrises from the boat.

Say goodbye to the rush of everyday life. On board there is nothing to organize and nowhere to be: the Eagle Ray Expeditions crew takes care of the boat, the kitchen and the logistics, and you only have to be there, present, with the sea and the wind. While you ride, he can head out on his wing.

I will be with you the whole time, like in your lessons, with a lot more water around us.
about.imageAlt: Lou, Expedition Leader and kite instructor with Eagle Ray Expeditions

season.title: The wind in season
season.text:
The season runs from November to March. The wind comes from the north and northwest, and around La Ventana it tends to fill in around noon and last until late afternoon.

Spot guides put the usual range at 10 to 25 knots, with stronger days when the north wind (El Norte) blows, in the 20 to 30 knot range. [Lou: confirm, and add the best months]

itinerary.title: Day by day
itinerary.intro:
A sample of how six days can go. The captain and Lou choose each day's anchorage and riding spot from the wind and the sea state, so read this as a rhythm, not a fixed route.

The 3-night trip follows the same rhythm over four days.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: La Paz → first anchorage at Espíritu Santo

moments.text: Airport pickup and private transfer to the marina. Welcome on board, and a short talk with Lou about the wind forecast for the week.
A short sail to the first anchorage. If the wind is up in the afternoon, her first session.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Espíritu Santo, from anchorage to anchorage

moments.text: Kite in the best wind window of the day, with the tender on the water. Snorkel, paddleboard and kayak off the boat in between.
A long lunch at anchor and a sail to the next bay.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Toward La Ventana, if the wind points that way

moments.text: La Ventana is one of the possible spots. The wind there tends to fill in during the afternoon, so we time the crossing for it.
We stay in the islands and ride another day.

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Around La Ventana or back in the islands

moments.text: A second riding day. Lou coaches her on the water, and the two of you ride.
A rest day: snorkel, paddleboard, a slow lunch.

days.label: Day 5
days.title: A longer day out toward Isla Cerralvo

moments.text: A possibility on the 5-night trip, only if conditions and Lou say yes. It is not a fixed activity.
One more day of riding in the best spot of the week.
Breakfast at anchor, a last swim, and the sail back to La Paz. Disembark at the marina and private transfer to the airport.

boats.title: The boat
boats.pricingText: Prices are for the whole boat and the two of you, in US dollars. They are valid for the kite season, December to April. Christmas, New Year and Holy Week dates on request.

options.name: Lagoon 450F
options.intro:
A 45-foot catamaran with four double cabins and four bathrooms, built in 2018 and refitted in 2024.

Why a catamaran works for kite: a wide deck to rig on, a stable boat at anchor, and the option to anchor close to shore. The flybridge, the inflatable dock and the tender make getting in and out of the water easy.

This boat or a similar one, subject to availability for your dates.
features: Air conditioning in every cabin and in the saloon

options.intro:
A 55-foot sailing monohull, for those who want to feel the boat heel under sail. It is also the lower-priced option.

The cockpit table seats ten, so lunch at anchor happens outside, and the swim platform lowers to the waterline. Below deck: three suites and three bathrooms.

crew.title: Your crew
crew.text:
Every expedition has a crew of three: a captain who knows these waters well, a chef who cooks with local produce and what the sea gives that week, and an Expedition Leader who looks after the group.

We choose them for their love of the sea and for how they share it with other people. They come from sailing, diving and hospitality (Ritz-Carlton, Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental).
crew.explainText:
An Expedition Leader is not a guide who follows a script, and not a host who serves the table. It is the Eagle Ray Expeditions person who stays with you the whole trip and answers for how it goes.

They know the group, decide with the captain when to swim and when to sail, look after everyone in the water, and take care of the details so you don't have to think about them.

That is the difference from chartering a boat with a crew: here someone is in charge of your experience, not only of the navigation. On this trip, that person is also her kite coach.
